about: Rest Mode quotations. Maintained by the app's administrator in this file. Only entries with status "approved" are shown. Every approved entry was checked word for word against the linked source on the date in verification.checked. Translations marked "app" were written for One Day and are labeled as such in the app; translations marked "published" are from the named public-domain edition.

text.en: There were times when I could not afford to sacrifice the bloom of the present moment to any work, whether of the head or hands. I love a broad margin to my life.
text.es: Había momentos en que no podía permitirme sacrificar la flor del momento presente a ningún trabajo, ni de la cabeza ni de las manos. Me gusta un margen amplio en mi vida.
text.it: C’erano momenti in cui non potevo permettermi di sacrificare il fiore del momento presente a nessun lavoro, né della testa né delle mani. Amo un ampio margine nella mia vita.
text.fr: Il y avait des moments où je ne pouvais me permettre de sacrifier la fleur de l’instant présent à aucun travail, ni de la tête ni des mains. J’aime laisser une large marge à ma vie.

source.title: Walden; or, Life in the Woods

text.en:
I loafe and invite my soul,
I lean and loafe at my ease observing a spear of summer grass.
text.es:
Holgazaneo e invito a mi alma,
me recuesto y holgazaneo a mis anchas observando una brizna de hierba de verano.
text.it:
Ozio e invito la mia anima,
mi appoggio e ozio a mio agio osservando un filo d’erba d’estate.
text.fr:
Je flâne et j’invite mon âme,
je m’accoude et flâne à mon aise en observant un brin d’herbe d’été.

verification.note: Spelling “loafe” is Whitman’s. The 1856 edition has a comma after “ease”; this entry follows the final edition.

text.en:
Come forth into the light of things,
Let Nature be your teacher.
text.es:
Sal a la luz de las cosas,
deja que la Naturaleza sea tu maestra.
text.it:
Vieni fuori nella luce delle cose,
lascia che la Natura sia la tua maestra.
text.fr:
Sors dans la lumière des choses,
que la Nature soit ton maître.

verification.note: Representative Poetry Online, from the 1798 first edition. The poem invites the reader to leave their books and go outdoors.

quotes.author: Psalm 23:2

text.en: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
text.es: En lugares de delicados pastos me hará yacer: Junto á aguas de reposo me pastoreará.
text.it: Egli mi fa giacere in verdeggianti paschi, mi guida lungo le acque chete.
text.fr: Il me fait reposer dans de verts pâturages, Il me dirige près des eaux paisibles.

quotes.rights: All four translations are in the public domain.

verification.note: Full verse in each translation, unchanged.

text.es: Hay que dar descanso a la mente.
text.fr: Il faut accorder du repos à l’esprit.

source.title: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquillity of Mind)

verification.note: First clause of the sentence. The rest of the sentence says rested minds rise better and keener; it is left out so the app makes no promise about results.

text.en: Let us spend one day as deliberately as Nature, and not be thrown off the track by every nutshell and mosquito’s wing that falls on the rails.
text.es: Pasemos un día tan deliberadamente como la Naturaleza, sin que nos saque del camino cada cáscara de nuez o ala de mosquito que cae sobre los rieles.
text.it: Trascorriamo un giorno con la stessa calma della Natura, senza farci sviare da ogni guscio di noce o ala di zanzara che cade sui binari.
text.fr: Passons une journée aussi posément que la Nature, sans nous laisser dérailler par chaque coquille de noix ou aile de moustique qui tombe sur les rails.

source.title: Walden; or, Life in the Woods
source.detail: chapter “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”

quotes.author: Ecclesiastes 3:1

text.en: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven
text.es: Para todas las cosas hay sazón, y todo lo que se quiere debajo del cielo, tiene su tiempo
text.it: Per tutto v’è il suo tempo, v’è il suo momento per ogni cosa sotto il cielo
text.fr: Il y a un temps pour tout, un temps pour toute chose sous les cieux

quotes.rights: All four translations are in the public domain.

verification.note: The verse ends with a colon because the list that follows continues it; the colon is left off for display. Reina-Valera capitalizes the first word as a chapter opening (“PARA”); shown in normal case.

text.en: Adopt the pace of nature: her secret is patience.

verification.note: Widely attributed, but the wording could not be found in the checked text of this edition.

text.en: Rest is not idleness, and to lie sometimes on the grass under trees on a summer’s day…

verification.note: The available scan of the book ended before this chapter, so the wording could not be checked.

text.la: Da requiem: requietus ager bene credita reddit

verification.note: Wording is correct, but in context it is advice on keeping a lover interested through absence. Using it as a message about rest would change its meaning.

text.fr: tout le malheur des hommes vient de ne savoir pas se tenir en repos dans une chambre

verification.note: Wording differs between editions (“se tenir” or “demeurer en repos”), and it frames rest through unhappiness. Not used.
